## Install

Nothing here is code-signed yet, so your system will ask you to confirm the first time.

| | File | First time |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows** | `BoardDock-3.1.0-win-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `…-portable.exe` (no install) | Choose **More info → Run anyway**. |
| **macOS** | `BoardDock-3.1.0-mac-….dmg` (open it and drag BoardDock into Applications) | Right-click the app and choose **Open**. |
| **Linux** | `BoardDock-3.1.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it, then run it) or the `.deb` (`sudo apt install ./BoardDock-3.1.0-linux-….deb`) | Nothing. |
| **In your browser** | [danmover.github.io/boarddock](https://danmover.github.io/boarddock) | Nothing is uploaded: it all runs in your browser. |

The desktop app does two things the browser can't: it opens Cadence Allegro `.brd` boards (with KiCad 10 or newer installed, free from kicad.org), and **Open plate** hands a plate to a slicer you have installed.

## From the first real print

This release fixes what the first printed rack (from v3.0.0) showed. The DIN rail clip worked well and is unchanged. The rest:

### The dock
- **Release button**: its rod was too tight in its tunnel, so it had to be forced in and the button broke. The tunnel now has 0.8 mm of play round the rod, a lead-in funnel and chamfers, and the rod's neck under the button is solid and filleted. It clicks in with two barbed fingers under a gate at the top of the tunnel.
- **Socket latch**: a holder popped out too easily. The latch pulled out because its nose sits off the spring's axis, so a pull tipped it out (the model has it slipping at about 10 N). It is now a long tapered spring with a deeper hook undercut 15°, so a pull draws the hook in: a 20 N pull moves it 0.4 of its 1.4 mm, and it slips only at about 69 N. It is also easier to use: 3.9 N to push a holder in (was 11 N) and 2.5 N on the button (was 3.8 N), at 0.85 % strain (was 1.4 %).
- **Tongue stoppers**: the small leaves that stopped a holder rattling, and the latch's stop post, hung on thin joints and snapped. They are gone. Two crush ribs on the tongue flatten to fit the first time it goes in, and a new check makes every stop and catch join its part at least 1.2 mm wide, inside its own print layer.

### Boards are held by spring clips only
- **Snap pins are gone.** The split pins in the mounting holes broke straight away. Every board is now held by spring clips on its edges, sized for the board (leaf length, catch and push from its size and weight). Where plugs take most of the edges, a **fixed ledge** goes on one side: the board slides under it and the clips opposite click over it. A mounting hole gets at most a plain locating pin, which grips nothing.
- **Hairpin clips** (the leaf folds back on itself) wherever a stretch of edge is 10 mm or less.
- The **Hold the board with** setting (Auto / Clips / Pins / Both) is gone; projects that asked for pins get clips. **Clip strength** (Firm or Gentle) stays.
- Every board in the library gets clips, each under 1 % strain when pressed in and none loaded once the board is in. The Pi Zero, whose edges are nearly all plugs, gets two hairpins and a ledge.

### Every clip is a spring that doesn't wear out
Every part that flexes is now checked against one rule, for PETG: at most 1 % strain at full deflection and at most 0.2 % while resting, with the hold coming from the hook's shape, not from pressure. Parts that didn't meet it were redesigned:
- **Plug caps** stand on tapered legs with rounded roots (at most 0.9 %, down from 1.2 %).
- **Holder hooks** on the DIN plate are tapered beams, and the plate's clip has a long shallow jaw ramp, an even 0.8 mm leaf 17 mm long and a gusseted stop.
- **Cable tags** are an open saddle held on by a 2.5 mm zip tie (the ties are in the shopping list); the old snap ring had to stretch 8 to 30 % round a stiff cable.
- **Back-to-back holders** are joined by a rigid pin and a U clip that slides onto its neck (0.84 %; the old split rivet reached 15 %).
- **Rail end blocks** are a 0.3 mm slip fit: their crush ribs would have flattened the first time and left the rail loose.

### Also
- Generic Marlin and Klipper start code counts as known, so those printers get **Slice and download all G-code** as the main button.

## Known limits

- **Nothing from this release has been printed yet.** The fixes above come from the model and its checks; the first reprint will tell.
- Nothing can clip a USB-serial adapter (docked or flat), a round board of about 20 mm lying flat, or a board docked on an edge crowded with plugs: the Check step says **Nothing clips this board in**.
- The Nano's 8 mm hairpin is over the limit in PLA; print it in PETG.
- The rail grip in the shoe rests under a small permanent preload (about 1 % strain), more than the resting rule allows. It is what holds the shoe on the rail, and the rail clip worked in the first print.
- A second J-Link for one board needs a ribbon of about 250 mm (a 30 cm ribbon; the Debug panel says so).
- Some connector sizes are still typical ones, with no public datasheet drawing to check them against.
